key_insight: A deep learning MRI biomarker mapped glioma infiltration beyond contrast-enhancing margins, reaching an independent test-set AUC of 0.942 after augmentation optimization.
clinical_relevance: The investigational infiltration maps may support surgical planning, radiotherapy targeting, and glioma burden assessment; this is imaging biomarker research, not drug discovery.
method: Trained a 3D convolutional neural network on multiparametric MRI patches.
Used localized glioma biopsies as histopathologic ground truth and peritumoral metastasis regions as non-tumor controls.
Applied patient-level cross-validation, independent testing, and optimized augmentation to generate voxel-wise infiltration maps.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 121 biopsy-localized samples from 56 glioma patients and 104 control samples from 26 metastasis patients; optimization increased test accuracy from 74.5% to 85.5% and AUC from 0.859 to 0.942 (p = 0.008).
watch_item: Prospective clinical utility remains unproven, and the abstract inconsistently reports the metastasis cohort size as 24 versus 26 patients.
paper_title: Biopsy-Validated Deep Learning Mapping of Glioma Infiltration Beyond Contrast Enhancement Using Multiparametric MRI
